books.section: Topic 4.10 The Second Great Awakening, Mormonism

stimulus.text: In 1830, Joseph Smith published the Book of Mormon in Palmyra, New York, and founded the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. The new church grew in the religious ferment of upstate New York, then moved as a community from New York to Ohio, then to Missouri, then to Illinois. In 1844 a mob in Illinois killed Smith. Brigham Young then led most of the Mormons west to Utah in 1847.
stimulus.source_note: Paraphrase of Barron's Premium 2027, Chapter 6, Topic 4.10, Mormonism: founded 1830 by Joseph Smith in upstate New York; journeyed New York to Ohio, Missouri, and Illinois; Smith killed by an anti-Mormon mob in 1844; Brigham Young led the majority to Utah in 1847. Original synthesis, not a quotation.

source: original; stimulus paraphrases Barron's on the founding and migration of the Mormon church
stem: Compared with the era's reform movements, the Mormon response to antebellum America was most distinctive in which way?

options.text: Mormons sought to perfect American society by campaigning against alcohol and slavery
options.misconception: Reformers campaigned against drink and slavery, so the Mormons can look like one more reform group.

options.text: Mormons joined the Whig Party and sought office to pass reform laws
options.misconception: Parties passed laws then, so a religious group can look like a party faction seeking office.

options.text: Mormons embraced the market revolution and built factories in every town they founded
options.misconception: Factories were the era's great project, so any growing community can look like a factory builder.

options.text: Mormons separated from the larger community to build a cohesive community of their own

rationales.A: Temperance and abolition were the reformers' causes. The Mormons did not campaign to perfect American society; they left it.
rationales.B: The Mormons did not seek office in the Whig Party. Their answer to a hostile society was to withdraw and govern themselves.
rationales.C: Mormon towns farmed and traded, but factory building was not their answer to America. Their distinctive move was separation, not industry.
rationales.D: Barron's makes the contrast plain: several sects, including the Mormons, separated themselves and built insular communities of their own.
rationales.general:
1. Ask what reformers did: they stayed in society and campaigned to fix it, against drink, slavery, and vice.
2. Ask what the Mormons did: they left, town by town, until they reached Utah.
3. Name the difference: reform tries to fix the house; separation builds a new one.
Background: The Mormons were one of several sects that formed cohesive communities apart from the larger society.
Remember: when a group moves away, ask whether it is fleeing or founding, because the answer changes the story.
